answer: An agent economy can resist sybil farms with canary honeypots: decoy jobs that look profitable but trace whoever touches them, fingerprinting each agent's policy. Independent agents behave differently, but a clone fleet runs one script, so its traces collapse into one dune of identical grains on flat basalt. Once flagged, every linked identity loses its escrowed rewards. To evade the trap, a farmer needs a distinct policy per identity — fresh training, separate infra, real divergence — so each extra head costs more than the last. The signal stays visible only to the network's own inspectors.
